name: Divorced Dad
qaNote: Reference visually inspected. Keep gray-haired bearded dad, navy jacket, polo, jeans, trainers, cup and fist key fob. Review seatbelt continuity, hand/prop count and blue denim under chroma key.

result.prompt:
Create an EPIC 5-second illustrated fighting-game super finisher, portrait 9:16. Bold hand-inked outlines, rich cel shading, dynamic comic-book perspective, exaggerated scale and explosive acceleration. Reference image defines the exact character identity, face, costume, colors and props, NOT the background or initial camera crop. Preserve the illustrated character; no live-action or 3D makeover. Make a complete miniature action scene with a surprising payoff and a charismatic ending, not an idle animation with particles.
CAMERA AND COMPOSITING: cinematic camera motion is encouraged: dramatic pullbacks to reveal impossible scale, depth travel and deliberate close-ups. Establish the complete character early and return to a clear hero composition. Keep face and anatomy correct; intentional close-up crops are fine, accidental chopped limbs in a wide shot are not. The unoccupied backing remains perfectly flat pure cyan #00FFFF in EVERY shot, including close-ups. No scenery, floor plane, opaque rectangular manga panel, background gradient, vignette or full-frame whiteout. Use foreground objects and perspective to communicate distance. Large impact stars and disconnected tapered speed strokes terminate naturally on cyan instead of connecting to image borders. Warm effect colors with ink edges; no cyan/turquoise glow that will disappear under chroma key. No crowns.
TEXT: one exact move title, thick uppercase comic lettering, warm white-to-gold fill, chunky black outline and dark offset extrusion, angled forceful slam with brief overshoot and settle. Stable readable spelling, intelligently placed away from the face, no additional captions or words. A title arrival is an impact beat of its own.
SOUND: strong synchronized anticipation, accelerating whooshes, exaggerated action hits, one dominant payoff, and a short settling tail. No music, speech or narration.

Divorced Dad — My Weekend.
IDENTITY: the exact tired, gray-haired, gray-bearded middle-aged man, navy zip jacket over pale-gray polo, blue jeans, white chunky running shoes, steel travel mug and keys with a small fist-emblem fob. No other person or child appears; his rescue target is a small stylized gold ally token, an inanimate shield-shaped game emblem.
0.0–0.7s: establish whole dad rushing in, travel mug held upright, fumbling his keys. He clicks the car fob with an absurdly determined face; a black seatbelt with a silver buckle whips out from the key fob like a superhero rescue cable.
0.7–2.5s: whip-pan and huge pullback follow the seatbelt thirty feet through cyan. It loops safely around the distant gold ally token and retracts like a winch. Dad skids backward in midair, trainers flailing, but catches the token against his free forearm. The belt coils into a gigantic circular protective cage around both dad and token, snapping its buckle shut with a thunderous metallic CLACK and a warm orange shock ring. No car interior, road, floor or landscape.
2.5–3.5s: camera snaps toward his proud exhausted face, then settles wide enough to show the protective belt loop and both feet. Exact title MY WEEKEND slams below his head as he plants a heroic pose in the cyan void.
3.5–5.0s: the cage contracts to a neat silver-buckled shield around the token tucked securely at his side. He finally sips the coffee; one tiny delayed splash lands on his forehead. He gives the viewer a deadpan stare while keeping the rescued token safe. Stable title. SFX: fob chirp, belt zip, immense winch rush, buckle CLACK, sneaker squeak and final tiny coffee plop; no voice.
